interest: Shows Irish efforts to dispel rumors of Japanese espionage, noting only four Japanese nationals lived in Ireland's twenty-six counties.
overview: Two 1942 cross-reference sheets on Japanese presence in neutral Ireland: an Irish Legation note that only four Japanese lived in the twenty-six counties, and a Brennan-Welles conversation on Japanese tourists.

people.name: Robert Brennan
people.role: Irish Minister to the United States

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording advice from the Irish Legation that only four Japanese nationals reside in the twenty-six counties of Ireland.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference (Nov 1942): the Irish Legation advises only four Japanese nationals reside in Ireland's twenty-six counties.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Axis Agents in Ireland

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a memorandum of conversation between Robert Brennan and Sumner Welles concerning Japanese tourists in Ireland.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Nov 1942 memo of conversation between Irish Minister Brennan and Under Secretary Welles on Japanese tourists in Ireland.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japanese Tourists in Ireland
